title: Customer-mapped usage CSV profiles + server-side preview service
creator: Asha Patel
description: Add a first-class feature to let customers define export 'CSV profiles' (column ordering, field selection, per-column transforms, null and quoting rules) and a server-side preview endpoint so customers can validate the CSV format before scheduling. This ticket covers backend services: profile CRUD, validation, preview runner that samples tenant usage records, and integration into the scheduled export worker pipeline so profiles are applied at export time. Goal: reduce customer support for custom CSV needs and avoid brittle per-tenant ad-hoc engineering; enable self-serve column mapping for common reporting cases.
acceptance_criteria: Customers can create/edit/delete CSV profiles via the Console API (profile stored in DB with versioning and audit metadata)
Preview endpoint returns a sample CSV (first N rows sampling strategy) within 5s for up to 1k sampled events and includes mapping/transform diagnostics
Scheduled exports apply the selected profile and produce CSVs that match the preview output schema for the same input snapshot
Profiles are validated server-side for malformed transforms, disallowed PII-revealing expressions, and size limits; validation failures surface as actionable errors in the Console
Audit log entries created for profile changes and export runs including profile version used (sufficient for compliance)
technical_notes: DB: add table 'csv_profiles' fields: id, tenant_id, name, columns (ordered list as JSON string), transforms (text), version, created_by, created_at, updated_at
Transform engine: use sandboxed QuickJS/WASM runtime to evaluate small mapping functions per-row; impose CPU/memory timeout and disallow network/FS
Preview runner: sample recent usage rows via existing usage-query API with deterministic reservoir sampling for stable previews
Export worker change: apply profile transforms as a streaming stage; preserve backpressure semantics and implement checkpointing per-file to support resumable uploads to S3
Security: static analyzer to reject transforms referencing forbidden fields (customer.metadata, internal_token, raw_request_body)
Performance: avoid materializing full dataset during scheduled run; transform stream should batch 256 rows and flush at size/time thresholds
Fallback: if transform fails mid-run, mark file as partial, create a manifest with error marker and create a rollback record to requeue affected shard with default profile
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (feature flag off): Backend schema + API endpoints behind feature flag; migrations deployed; QuickJS runtime bundled on workers
Phase 2 (alpha customers): Enable for 3 pilot tenants (support team + 2 customers) to validate transforms and preview UX
Phase 3 (gradual rollout): Ramp to 25% of scheduled exports with profile selected; monitor error rate, CPU usage, S3 object success rate
Phase 4: Global enable by default, deprecate legacy per-tenant ad-hoc exports after 3 months with migration guide
test_plan: Unit tests for profile validation logic and transform sandbox boundaries
Integration tests: end-to-end preview -> scheduled run -> S3 object compare for deterministic sample dataset
Load tests: run 100 simultaneous profile-applied exports with 10M rows total across workers to validate memory bounds and throughput
Security fuzz tests: inject malicious transform payloads to ensure sandbox timeouts and static rejects work
Canary: run on dedicated test pool using customer-shaped telemetry and validate observability dashboards
